Hi Maria, 

The rental vs. leasing set-up does not affect the reclassification assessment. We just need to know it in order to make the correct assessment regarding licenses and permits as this type of car rental market is regulated in Sweden and there are different licenses and permits depending on the set-up but our policy team should be able to figure this out once we have informed them of the set-up. On top of my head I think we need to operate this from the local entity due to licensing requirements but this is also to be confirmed. If it is operated from the local entity then we may have to update our corporate purpose as well. TBC. 

Regarding the reclassification risk it has previously been deemed to be low in the Nordics in the RH vertical because Bolt’s business model is the same or similar as the model operated by TTO’s. However, we are planning on initiating an in-depth assessment of the market as there are a lot of movements and new features that could affect our previous assessment on this. 

Nevertheless, based on the information we have so far we would need to ensure that the usual safeguards are put in place when it comes to reclassification: 

* Rental/Lease should be handled as a separate service from our other services, i.e. separate agreement and full compensation based on market standard. 
* Not limited to specific drivers as this service must be kept separate from our driver scores or other rating criteria. No beneficial treatment for drivers that rent cars via us.

Basically, it needs to be treated as a separate service in all aspects as one of the main criteria for reclassification is Sweden is the provision of work tools and if the cars under any circumstances would be deemed to be a benefit to the drivers or that Bolt provides the work tools then this could put Bolt in the spotlight for any authorities /regulators but also potentially mean that individual drivers claim that Bolt is their employer as work tools are provided by Bolt (in addition to the other factors that put us at risk for reclassification such as acceptance rate blocking, handling the payments on behalf of the different parties etc.). 

Let me know if you need any additional details on this.

Hello Mattias, 

The procedure for Germany will pretty much stay the same, we just updated the templates that CS agents will use with drivers. This is how it works:

* The report comes in ([vehicle accident|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2407628971/Driver+In+Major+Vehicle+Related+Accident+Ride-hailing#Driver-in-Vehicle-Accident-Causing-Injury-or-Structural-Damage]/[unfit vehicle|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2404581840/Driver+Operating+in+Fraudulent+Manner+Ride-hailing#Not-Fit-for-Purpose-Vehicle-Use])
* The driver gets blocked and the investigation starts;
* CS Safety uses the templates in the screenshot (these are in German)
* Once the tool is filled in, your team gets a notification in #se-safety-ops-blocking
** The notification would look like the one you see in the screenshot
** You decide whether the vehicle should be blocked, handle communication with the FO, unblock the vehicle, etc.) 
* When the investigation is over, the CS Safety agent removes the block from the driver
** No need to wait for evidence of car repair from the CS side, as that part would be handled between you and the fleet owner 

[Here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~62f27f32d49df231b6297bd4/pages/4361356159/DE+Safety+Ops+Blocking+Process+for+Local+Ops] you can find German Ops team instructions to contact the fleet owner, block the vehicle, etc. (it’s done by them, I asked if I could share it with you). 

If this solution works for you, we would just need to have the templates translated into Swedish. 

----

Another solution we have in place in Portugal is similar but without Investigative blocks in case of an accident/unfit vehicle. You’d receive a notification that the vehicle might need to be blocked but this is it. In PT this is done purely due to new regulations, but my suggestion is to keep the investigative blocks. 

----

If you’d like to discuss this further, feel free to schedule a sync next week. p

Cheers, 

Alessandro

+*Amendments to Legislation*+

*Legislation:* Working Environment Act 

The new rules will enter into force on 1 April 2023 (with a three months transitional period for contracts already entered into). For already concluded agreements, many of the changes will not take effect until 1 July 2023.

*The changes entail as follows:*

The right for firms to hire from staffing companies when the work is of a temporary nature will be revoked.

Employers will be stripped of the option to hire from staffing agencies based on the temporary character of the job. This means that employers can only hire workers as temporary replacements for another person or persons. However, the Ministry is permitted to adopt special rules on time-limited hiring of health personnel, in addition to advisers and consultants with specialist expertise.

*In what situations will it be possible to hire from staffing companies?*

* For temporary replacement of permanent employees during holidays, leave of absence, sick leave and similar situations.
* Work training as for instance trainees.
* For participants in Labor market schemes under the auspices of or in cooperation with the Labour and Welfare Administration (NAV).
* For athletes, trainers, referees and other leaders within organized sports
* Upon agreement with employees’ union representatives, if the company is bound by a collective agreement with a trade union of a certain size.

*Options for companies in need of increased labor for a limited period:*

* Increase the number of permanent employees
* Hire employees from companies which main purpose is not being a staffing company
* Employ workers temporarily directly in the company
* Divide the work by entering into construction agreements with clients.

The restrictions on hiring workers from temporary-work agencies will mean that companies may have to obtain staff by other means such as: 

* Entering into direct permanent or temporary employment with the employee, make use of subcontractors and independent contractors, or enter into special agreements with trade unions on hiring from staffing agencies where possible.

*The right to permanent employment is strengthened.* The new rules find that those who have worked with the same business for more than three years will have the right to a permanent direct job with the employer they are placed to. 

Trade unions' right to collectively institute legal proceedings in the event of illegal hire from temporary-work agencies have been reintroduced. The trade unions can institute legal proceedings irrespective of the (un)willingness of the employees involved.

My numbers are estimated if the most active drivers only select cash-orders for a day (& their balance is 0) they will not get blocked in 24 hours. But with 60% in-app rate this is highly unlikely because I’d assume the most active drivers don’t care about payment method much. 

Regarding CS tickets this is up to the local team to educate the drivers how the balance works & what is blocking thresholds, how to make us a payment etc. From your message in Slack you’ve estimated the limits to enable a driver to ride for 4-6 weeks without getting blocked but on a global scale this period is too large. Hi [~accountid:619e455ab43d5b006a05c173] just wanted to add for Norway that the government recently adopted amendments to the legislation regarding the classification of employees and independent contractors, intending to make it easier for contractors to determine whether they are entitled to employee status under the law. Effective 1 January 2024, the definition of "employee" will be changed to "anyone who performs work for and is subordinate to another". Furthermore, *a presumption rule* will be introduced stating that employee status should be assumed unless the contractor can demonstrate that a contractual relationship (rather than an employment relationship) is "overwhelmingly likely". As a result, the engaging entities will be required to provide strong evidence of a contractual relationship. Failure to meet the evidential standard will result in the contractor being classified as an employee. 

Based on this we need to be careful when we rent/lease cars to drivers in Norway as it needs to be evident that this is a completely separate set-up. One of the factors for a contractor relationship to exists is that the contractor uses their own work tools.

Hi [~accountid:61151976ec92ab007046ccb7] [~accountid:627b6b918395420069681f70], 

Please confirm if you still want to explore any solutions with Adecco. As mentioned by you earlier, there have been changes in the legislation that limit the options for Bolt to lease workers from temporary work agencies in Norway. Please see a summary of the legislative changes below: 

--

+*Amendments to Legislation*+

*Legislation:* Working Environment Act 

The new rules will enter into force on 1 April 2023 (with a three months transitional period for contracts already entered into). For already concluded agreements, many of the changes will not take effect until 1 July 2023.

*The changes entail as follows:*

The right for firms to hire from staffing companies when the work is of a temporary nature will be revoked.

Employers will be stripped of the option to hire from staffing agencies based on the temporary character of the job. This means that employers can only hire workers as temporary replacements for another person or persons. However, the Ministry is permitted to adopt special rules on time-limited hiring of health personnel, in addition to advisers and consultants with specialist expertise.

*In what situations will it be possible to hire from staffing companies?*

* For temporary replacement of permanent employees during holidays, leave of absence, sick leave and similar situations.
* Work training as for instance trainees.
* For participants in Labor market schemes under the auspices of or in cooperation with the Labour and Welfare Administration (NAV).
* For athletes, trainers, referees and other leaders within organized sports
* Upon agreement with employees’ union representatives, if the company is bound by a collective agreement with a trade union of a certain size.

*Options for companies in need of increased labor for a limited period:*

* Increase the number of permanent employees
* Hire employees from companies which main purpose is not being a staffing company
* Employ workers temporarily directly in the company
* Divide the work by entering into construction agreements with clients.

The restrictions on hiring workers from temporary-work agencies will mean that companies may have to obtain staff by other means such as: 

* Entering into direct permanent or temporary employment with the employee, make use of subcontractors and independent contractors, or enter into special agreements with trade unions on hiring from staffing agencies where possible.

*The right to permanent employment is strengthened.* The new rules find that those who have worked with the same business for more than three years will have the right to a permanent direct job with the employer they are placed to. 

Trade unions' right to collectively institute legal proceedings in the event of illegal hire from temporary-work agencies have been reintroduced. The trade unions can institute legal proceedings irrespective of the (un)willingness of the employees involved.

--

*CZ - the contract types you describe are generally permissible, provided that general contract principles and rules governing advertising are followed.*

* I believe that the issue of the contractual arrangement between you and your partner entities must be governed by the principle of autonomy of will as your contractual matter. Such contracts will most likely fall under so-called innominate contracts, as they are not a specific type of contract regulated by law. Therefore, if there is no violation of general principles of private law (e.g. regarding an unreasonable contractual penalty, the conclusion of a contract due to coercion, etc.), then I generally consider such a contract to be permissible. However, it is also possible that such an arrangement will contain the character of a different contractual type and then the contract will be governed by the relevant provisions to this extent - due to the described uniqueness of the relationship, I rather do not expect this.
* The advertisement must also meet the requirements in the area of protection against unfair competition - it must not be misleading, it must not be a prohibited comparative advertisement, etc. However, these matters concern the advertisement itself, not your contractual relationship with partner drivers. In the same way, advertising must meet the conditions set out in the level of public regulation (especially Act No. 40/1995 Coll. on the regulation of advertising). Advertising must not disrupt public order and traffic on the roads. But again, this is about regulating the result - the form of advertising that you place on partner vehicles. The contractual relationships that lead to this placement are a matter of private law applied independently of public law regulation.

While the previous version of the rider lost items process included the possibility of sharing the driver’s phone number with the rider, this is no longer possible - as we cannot share a person’s contact details without their explicit permission. This was confirmed by the Privacy team when we last updated this process.

When it comes to CSAT, I think these are very important aspects that may impact it:

* how well we inform the rider of the _realistic_ possibilities of getting back their item and how this process is going;
* how well both parties (rider and driver) are able to communicate with each other and coordinate the retrieval of the item.

*About informing the rider* - the current process pretty much keeps the rider in the dark after we try to contact the driver. We can improve the rider’s experience by informing them whether we contacted the driver and if the item is with them. Here, I think it’s also important to clearly establish the understanding for the rider on how much CS can help them with getting their item back. I’m currently looking at how we can improve this issue. 🙂 

*About communication between both parties* - if there’s a language barrier between the rider and driver, asking the driver to take time to drop the item off at a local police station causes additional friction for the driver. I’m not sure if that’s a better experience than what’s happening now. Instead, we may encourage the driver to communicate in a written format (via SMS) so that they can translate the messages.

Essentially, I don’t see the language barrier as a CS process issue - instead, I’d look into whether drivers are receiving proper training about communicating with riders in case they speak different languages. You can certainly challenge me on this topic if you think otherwise. 🙂

 qr_code_change_ts as (
  select vehicle_id, created qr_code_change_ts
  from ng_rental.rental_fleet_vehicle_change_log
 where type = 'uuid'
 and created_date >=date'2023-01-01'
 ),
 log as (
select e.id, e.created,e.vehicle_id,e.from_state ,e.to_state, qrc.qr_code_change_ts
from ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event e
join ng_rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on e.search_category_id =sc.id 
join ng_public.admin_system_city c on c.id =sc.city_id --and c.name not in ('Lisbon','Warsaw','Kyiv','Hamburg','Cologne','Stuttgart','Frankfurt','Zagreb','Wroclaw','Dnipro','Braga','Vilnius','Munich','Vila Nova de Gaia','Poznan','Berlin','Lviv','Bucharest','Riga','Bielefeld')
left join qr_code_change_ts qrc 
	on qrc.vehicle_id=e.vehicle_id 
where e.created_date >=date'2023-01-01'
and e.type='state'
and (
	(e.from_state in ('lost','operational') and e.to_state = 'collected') 
	or 
	(e.from_state='being_serviced' and e.to_state = 'collected')
	)
order by e.vehicle_id  asc, e.id, e.created asc
)
select --*
date_trunc('week',CREATED),count(distinct vehicle_id),1.0*avg(time_till_next_event)/60
from (
select t.* from 
(
select *,
lead(from_state,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc) next_from_state,
lead(to_state,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc) next_to_state,
lead(created,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc) next_created,
case when qr_code_change_ts between l.created and lead(l.created,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc) then 1 else 0 end qr_code_change_happened,
date_diff('minute',l.created,lead(l.created,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc)) time_till_next_event
from log l 
) t
left join relevant_services rs on t.vehicle_id=rs.vehicle_id and rs.created between t.created and t.next_created 
)
where 
	from_state in ('lost','operational') 
	and to_state='collected' 
	and next_from_state='being_serviced' 
	and next_to_state='collected'
	and qr_code_change_happened=0
	and time_till_next_event<7200
group by 1
order by 1 asc{code}

  from ng_rental.rental_fleet_vehicle_change_log
 where type = 'uuid'
 and created_date >=date'2023-01-01'
 ),
 log as (
select e.id, e.created,e.vehicle_id,e.from_state ,e.to_state, qrc.qr_code_change_ts
from ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event e
join ng_rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on e.search_category_id =sc.id 
join ng_public.admin_system_city c on c.id =sc.city_id --and c.name not in ('Lisbon','Warsaw','Kyiv','Hamburg','Cologne','Stuttgart','Frankfurt','Zagreb','Wroclaw','Dnipro','Braga','Vilnius','Munich','Vila Nova de Gaia','Poznan','Berlin','Lviv','Bucharest','Riga','Bielefeld')
left join qr_code_change_ts qrc 
	on qrc.vehicle_id=e.vehicle_id 
where e.created_date >=date'2023-01-01'
and e.type='state'
and (
	(e.from_state in ('lost','operational') and e.to_state = 'collected') 
	or 
	(e.from_state='being_serviced' and e.to_state = 'collected')
	)
order by e.vehicle_id  asc, e.id, e.created asc
)
select --*
date_trunc('week',qr_code_change_ts),count(distinct vehicle_id),1.0*avg(time_till_next_event)/60
from (
select t.* from 
(
select *,
lead(from_state,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc) next_from_state,
lead(to_state,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc) next_to_state,
lead(created,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc) next_created,
case when qr_code_change_ts between l.created and lead(l.created,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc) then 1 else 0 end qr_code_change_happened,
date_diff('minute',l.created,lead(l.created,1) over (partition by l.vehicle_id, qr_code_change_ts order by l.created asc, l.id asc)) time_till_next_event
from log l 
) t
left join relevant_services rs on t.vehicle_id=rs.vehicle_id and rs.created between t.created and t.next_created 
)
where 
	from_state in ('lost','operational') 
	and to_state='collected' 
	and next_from_state='being_serviced' 
	and next_to_state='collected'
	and qr_code_change_happened=1
	and time_till_next_event<7200
group by 1
order by 1 asc{noformat}

PURE ADVERTISING

* In order to legally provide advertising and marketing services an entity (natural person - entrepreneur or legal entity) is required to be registered for subject of business “Advertising, marketing, photography and information services, market research and public opinion”.
* Therefore, to legally operate the business, the taxi service providers will have to expand their subject of business to include advertising and marketing services.

 CAMPAIGN

Regardless of the above, both the campaign alternative and the advertising alternative must comply with advertising legislation - below is more detailed advise:



* The general requirements for advertising are primarily regulated by the Advertising Act and the Code of Ethics for Advertising Practice. 
** According to the provision § 3 par. (1) of the Advertising Act: *Advertising must not*
*** *a) contain anything that disgraces the human dignity, insults national feeling or religious feeling as well as any discrimination on basis of sex, race and social origin,*
*** *b) to propagate violence, vandalism or vulgarity and entice to unlawful acts or agree with it,*
*** *c) present nakedness of human body in scandalous way,*
*** *d) present products that damage the environment or products harmful to life or health of the people, animals or plants without specific and clear warning in advance,*
*** *e) threat physical health and mental health of citizen,*
*** *f) to present food and nutritional supplements as if they had the effects of medicines,*
*** *g) contain personal data, data on property relations of persons without their prior consent,*
*** *h) refer to statements made by other persons without their prior consent,*
*** *i) interfere with the rights of others without their consent,*
*** *(j) abuse the trust of minors, in particular*
***   *i. encourage behavior which may endanger their health, mental development, or moral development,*
***    *ii. display them in dangerous situations.*
* According to the provision § 3 par. (2) of the Advertising Act: *Advertising must meet the requirements* for public speech, adhere to the principles of language culture, grammar and spelling rules, rules of pronunciation *of the Slovak language* and established professional terminology.
* In connection with the above-mentioned legal provision, it is important to state that advertising must comply with the provisions of the State Language Act, according to which: All signs, advertisements and notices intended to inform the public, particularly in retail shops, sporting facilities, restaurants, in streets, by and above roads, at airports, bus stations and railway stations, as well as in public transport vehicles, shall be presented in the state language. If they contain the text in other languages, the texts in another language shall be presented after the text in the state language and shall be contentually identical with the state language text. The text in another language shall be presented in the same or smaller font than the state language text. (provision § 8 (6) of the State Language Act).
* According to the above, the advertisement must be stated first in the Slovak language and then in the English language, while the content must be identical in both languages and the advertisement in the English language must be in the same or smaller font as the text of the advertisement in the Slovak language.
* *The abovementioned requirement does not apply to the trade name, trademark, and to the use of the name and surname, which are part of the sign, advertisement and notice intended to inform the public, and to some customary expressions in a foreign language, which are usually used together with the trademark in the text of advertisements, are known to the wider public and are part of advertising.* 
* According to the provision § 3 par. (5) of the Advertising Act: Advertising must not be disseminated if it is contrary to good morals, presents products whose production, sale, provision, or use are prohibited, or if it does not meet the requirements of a special regulation. 
* According to the provision § 3 par. (6) of the Advertising Act: Advertising must not present products or services, the unauthorized manipulation of which is prohibited by special regulations.
* Just for your information, there is as well a specific regulation for:
** *Comparative advertising;*
** *Advertising of alcoholic beverages;*
** *Advertising of tobacco products;*
** *Advertising of weapons and ammunition;*
** *Advertising of medicines;*
** *Advertising of infant formulas and subsequent supplementary formulas.*
* For the sake of completeness, we should mention another legal regulation dealing with advertising. It is the Code of Ethics for Advertising Practice, which is issued by the Advertising Council.
* The purpose of the Code of Ethics is to codify the ethical principles of advertising practice in Slovakia and accordingly contribute to ensuring that advertising in the Slovak Republic best serves advertisers and consumers, meets the ethical aspects of advertising required by the public, is above all true, honest, and decent and in the form of this Code of Ethics, respect the internationally recognized principles of advertising practice developed by the International Chamber of Commerce.

As I can see, this is a very market-specific/local issue. Since the training team has to follow long-term planning, we only have limited capacity to create new trainings from scratch. Therefore, I just wanted to point out that the Training team generally prioritizes global requests or requests with a large business impact. That is why apart from specific and observable behaviors your agents would have after completing the training it is also important *to specify your business goal (impact) in numbers.* This is what I mean by that: ([Before you request a Training -> Analyze the issue|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CS/pages/3729326359/Requesting+a+new+training]):

# Determine performance problem using data and your own observations.

# The problem statement shouldn’t refer to knowledge, e.g. _agents don’t know HP processes_.
# Instead, focus on *specific and observable* *behaviors* or lack thereof, e.g. _outsourced agents escalate X type of tickets to in-house, but these are not HP cases and outsourced agents should handle them on their own._

# Identify the impact of the issue on business.

# Example: _Outsourced agents escalate X type of tickets to in-house, but these are not HP cases and outsourced agents can handle them on their own. Because of that, total resolution time for these tickets is X (is high)._

# *Set a business goal you’d like to achieve.*

# *Example of correct business goal:* *_Total resolution time will decrease by 10% by the end of Q2 2022 as agents from Majorel who support the UK solve given cases on their own._*

*Template for setting a business goal*
*A measure we already use will increase / decrease*
*number % by date*
*as people in a specific group do something*

In your case, I'd think about it this way:

{quote}*problem statement -* OPS doesn’t have headcount to verify headcount on a daily basis -> _how many cases are we talking about daily/weekly/monthly?_
*impact -* faster support for new courier leads, therefore more supply for customers -> _how much would the AHT and FRT be shortened?_
*business goal -* more supply -> _how many more couriers could we add to the supply weekly/monthly?_{quote}

Thank you for the call last week! I wanted to summarize the questions, initial answers (for your official review) and next steps. Looking forward to aligning on how to effectively partner up on this:

*Question #1:* Can we use the GH automated extension of consent to store candidate data beyond 3 years? Would we then also be able to contact them throughout that period?
*Initial answer:* We can use it to extend storing of their data. We can combine this with consent to contact them, but the wording and process for this needs to be designed (see next steps).
*Next steps:* Confirm text of consent (to allow also contact extension) + process

*Question #2:* If candidates did not give consent to be considered for future opportunities, can we freely move them between roles?
*Initial answer:* This should be fine but we need to add transparency about this to the privacy notice
*Next steps:* Review privacy notice + add a clause to allow to move candidates

*Question #3:* If candidates did not give consent to be considered for future opportunities, can we still contact them if it's the same requisition they applied for (but have previously been rejected)?
*Initial answer:* No if we don't have consent their consent. If this is exactly the same role then it could be another case (tbc)
*Next steps:* Confirm what are the rules to qualify as "the same role" (same req? or just same role name?). Confirm how we can creatively reach out to them while maintaining compliance (for example via LinkedIn vs email).

*Question #4:* Can we collect consent to be considered for future opportunities from already rejected candidates?
*Initial answer:* TBC - we have their data for 3 years, but we need to work out how to do this
*Next steps:* double check & verify wording of consent email & how to track this + check "gray area" of using their data and contacting them on LinkedIn

*Question #5:* Do we need to link to our privacy policy in the 1st message to candidates?
*Initial answer:* Answered in thread above
*Next steps:* Clarify cases where this needs to be shared + process

*Question #6:* Can we maintain candidate blacklists? If so, do they need to follow the retention periods?
*Initial answer:* May be under our legitimate interest, but we need more info (see next steps)
*Next steps:* Silja to share form for us to fill with details why this is necessary, how we keep this list secure, how we maintain it, delete it

*Question #7:* Is creating candidate prospects in Greenhouse GDPR compliant?
*Initial answer:* We need to ask consent to add them as a prospect (if PII is stored)
*Next steps:* Clarify wording & process of consent. Confirm whether we can do this via LI since we need to log the consent somehow.

*Question #8:* Can the above consent be opt-out vs opt-in?
*Initial answer:* Needs to be opt-in, but sometimes we could use legitimate interest - but the data prospect needs to understand why the data is in our system
*Next steps:* Confirm & clarify cases where it could be legitimate interest and thus no opt-in needed

The Trial Balance document you indeed show the debit amount as 24k, but the transactions report only shows you the value of 268.84 for the transaction sum. This is occurring due to an intercompany transaction for inter company shipments.

!image-20230502-220452.png|width=50%!

The report Bolt Inventory Transaction accounting is run per company, therefore it returns all the transactions associated with the company that *initiates* the business document, i.e. the inventory shipment. 

For the Inventory Shipment where we have local billing (so transferred from Bolt Operations OU), this then produces a CR for 1350 Inventory account, and DR for 2111 (Trade Payments Intragroup EE) account.

On the transaction, it produces an intercompany journal entry to then do the following for Bolt Operations:

DR 1350 0.96
CR 2111 0.96

Then for the local entity it produces an intercompany journal entry:

DR 1350 0.96
CR 2112 0.96

!image-20230509-153414.png|width=2484,height=1293!

!image-20230509-153530.png|width=2533,height=1269!

Each shipment line transaction produces it’s owner journal, which results in lots of data I understand. 



TLDR; (thinking of [~accountid:60f2a718f749c4006829d8dd] here); The Shipment Transaction is assigned to Bolt Operations as the company which originates the transaction, and intercompany journal entry is produced on same journal entry therefore it does not show up in the custom report, but displays accurately in the Trial Balance. The transaction belongs to the originating company.

Since basket model data needs to be consistent, but it’s split across different tables, we want to make sure that when reading from those tables, the data is in sync. It belongs to the same basket version.

Reading inconsistent data (dirty reads) could end up in {color:#ff5630}*persisting inconsistent data*{color}, although, a good observation is that we always check for version matching when we save the data. Namely, if the basket model version at read time (assigned to previousVersion prop) isn’t the same as the basket.version on the db, we drop the update. {color:#36b37e}*This seems to cover the “persisting inconsistent data” concern.*{color}

Reading inconsistent data could end up in {color:#ff5630}*throwing business errors that are not valid / appropriate*{color}. … what errors could we have? … However, having {color:#4c9aff}*prices as functions*{color}, and {color:#4c9aff}*saving discounted prices closer to the entity price*{color}, to ensure consistent / atomic reads, would guarantee a consistent basket model on its own, though it {color:#ff5630}*could be different from what the user expects*{color}, smth like eventual consistency. This last aspect should be covered on updates by checking the basket version, as stated above.

Regarding the eventual consistency observed by the user, for requests that only serve data, I believe this is not desirable, and we can either avoid it by using locks, or a confirmation extra read to confirm that the basket version hasn’t changed. {color:#ffc400}*Which one is cheaper?*{color} But also, how would we recover from a changed version in this case, since we only wanted to present data.

h2. *Requested process change*

*The process scenario in question:* Rider didn’t pay or paid less (possibly - but may be all scenarios covered in the process)

*Issue:* We don’t contact the rider to get their side of the story

*Results of the issue:* Most of the drivers' compensation requests get processed, causing high costs

*Desired change:* Add a step on the 1st, 2nd and 3rd reports for Nigeria requiring the Rider to be sent a ticket informing them of the unpaid trip

*Goal:* Reduce costs due to driver compensations for this issue

h2. *Request validation*

Here’s when we compensate the drivers in Nigeria and when we don’t (based on the current [CS process|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015016234] and the local [compensation guidelines|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013479479]):

* *We compensate the driver if:*
** There’s an overcharge caused by incorrect or estimated upfront pricing (this is not the driver’s fault):
*** automation compensates 50% of the ride value
*** if automation wasn't applied - 100% compensation by CS
** There’s no overcharge:
*** automation compensates 50% of the ride value + CS should compensate the remaining 50% manually
*** if automation wasn’t applied - 100% compensation by CS
* *We don’t compensate the driver if:*
** There’s an overcharge caused by the driver’s behaviour.

The ticket requester mentioned adding a step to reach out to the rider for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd reports in Nigeria. To achieve the goal (reducing driver compensations), such instructions would need to be earlier in the process (before the driver is compensated).

*Some questions to clarify if and how we can update the process:*

# Does the ticket requester talk about _Rider didn’t pay or paid less_ scenario or all compensations covered in this process?
# What is the value of contacting the rider - what can the rider tell us that would make us reconsider the driver compensation?
# If there’s value in what the rider may tell, should we consider introducing the step globally - given that it’s the second driver issue based on the inquiry volume?

Hi Team, 

After the review of [the EE fleet models|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1w5IbUtz-FeiH2mA88SflkkeaOZPrGlh1PiuWUrRRgbc/edit], the following *problem* was identified: all incomes of drivers' who rent cars from the fleets (not being employed by it) are sent to the fleets. Such transactions are unjustified and lack legal basis. 

*The solution:* introduction of the *car rental payment split feature* that works in the following way (general overview):

# Every week (by Friday unless the local team set’s a different day) the fleet enters via the Fleet portal the amount it is willing to receive for car rental from driver’s revenue in a particular week.
# The drivers receive a weekly message that part of their earnings will be deducted in favor of the fleet. 
# The driver can dispute the deduction, therefore, Bolt cannot guarantee that the fleet will receive the payment. If the deduction is approved by the driver, the payment to the fleets is made on the same day as payouts to drivers (usually Mondays unless the local team set’s a different day)
# If the driver's earnings in a particular week are insufficient to cover fleets claim, Bolt pays the fleet on the driver's behalf. Bolt deducts owned amounts from the driver's next week's earnings.
# A weekly reconciliation report that reflects successful and unsuccessful set-off transactions shall be available on the Fleet portal. 

*Next steps:*

# *FINANCE* 

[~accountid:624469dd45ece00069c967bd] please approve that we can proceed with the payment split feature in Estonia provided:

* Payments to fleets are fully automated. Bolt employees cannot do manual adjustments to drivers balances. 
* Payments to fleets are made by the same Bolt entity that is making the payments to drivers.
* Payments to fleets are made upon receipt of driver's authorization (covered by the below authorization form).
* The local team ensures that fleets are reputable companies (perform business legitimately; have all required licenses; don't mislead drivers etc).

*2. LEGAL*

* All the fleets that currently receive all drivers' incomes for car rental, but are not employing drivers shall sign a new [*Fleet management portal access agreement*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FYQ5T5aIsNBqTkUk9Lod04206TMzGoCg/edit]. Currently, these fleets are bound by T&C for drivers - these contractual relations will be terminated by the new agreement. 
* All drivers who rent cars from fleets and whose incomes are sent to the fleet will sign [*the authorization form* |https://docs.google.com/document/d/18Vlv7NAt3B3Q0GB1icSzKQ3lwrKn61hZ/edit]authorizing Bolt to make the deductions from their earnings in favour of the fleet.

*3. LOCAL TEAM* 

While we are awaiting [~accountid:624469dd45ece00069c967bd] approval, the local team [~accountid:5d528d1b8d88e50c1d7055a0] [~accountid:626bc237bae0c1006fadfd63] [~accountid:5d3b12432acc2d0c6219ff80] please: 

* appoint the local owner for this project.
* get acquainted with the above information, check the shared agreement (please read clause 1.1. - 1.7 of the new fleet agreement) and the authorization form. 
* discuss your questions and the technical implementation of the feature with the product and life-cycling teams. 
* you may start drafting notifications for fleets and drivers where the new set-up is explained (a new agreement/form will be attached to this notification). Once the draft is ready, I can review it
* Think about any specific fleet obligation or cooperation particularities between Bolt and fleets in EE you would like to cover by the agreement. Let me know if there are any and I will think about the suitable clause to be added to the fleet agreement.

With apologies from the external advisor who had capacity issues, here is their feedback (better late than never!):

_It is our view that_ *_Bolt should not be liable towards the VAT Department for the fact that the drivers may have been obliged to collect VAT on transportation services provided to passengers_* _in Malta and failed to do so, in practice, because the Bolt system categorised them incorrectly and the invoice issued on behalf of the particular driver did_ +_not_+ _include VAT on the transportation system provided._

_I have just had a further call with the VAT Department and all is clear as per the below:_

# _Item 11, Second Schedule to the VAT Act, provides that_ 

_When a supply is made through an intermediary who acts in the name and for the account of another person that supply shall be treated as a supply made by that other person._

_The official I spoke to confirmed my understanding that since the receipts issued by your system makes it clear that the provider of the transportation system is the driver – as it includes the driver’s details, his VAT number etc. – then the supply of the transportation service should be deemed to be made by the driver, not Bolt._

2. _Following from the above, article 20 of the VAT Act further provides that in principle,_ 

_the payment of the tax on a taxable supply shall be the liability of the person who makes the supply_.  In this case, the person making the supply is the driver and therefore the obligation to collect and pay on the VAT due on the rides is of the driver, not of Bolt.

_On that basis,_ *_we confirm our view that the VAT Department should not be in a position to take any action against Bolt to recover VAT (or any interest/penalties on that unpaid VAT)_* _on the rides where the drivers have not charged VAT due to the “incorrect” invoices being issued by the system._

I hope that this has addressed all of the concerns on this topic? If anything is incorrect or if there are any further queries - please could you let me know in the next week (as I will be going off on maternity leave soon).

Given the overall contractual set up, in case of any regulatory intervention, the partner could still be deemed a data controller (and not a processor), however the risk associated with that is mostly on partner’s side. 

In this specific scenario, given that (a) the Partner clearly has very different interpretation of the set up; and (b) it results in overall low-to-medium risk for Bolt, from privacy side we can agree to proceed with proposed data processing agreement. However please note that this would translate to different obligations/responsibilities allocation than with our standard model, mainly:

* Bolt would be responsible for the processing carried out by the Partner in the course of this agreement (Bolt could seek redress from the partner, however it would be ultimately the liable entity);
* data protection complaints/requests from the data subjects lodged by the end-users in connection with their Starbucks order would have to be processed by Bolt;
* the Partner can be audited by Bolt (as set out in the GDPR and proposed contract), it should also inform Bolt about any incidents related to the processed personal data.

Please confirm if this change and proposed terms are acceptable from the commercial perspective.

I have also reviewed data processing agreement proposed by the Partner- please see the document with the edits attached. 



Finally, please note that this deviation from our standard approach doesn’t mean that we want to replicate this set up with other partners or change our overall approach - for future partnerships we will continue with controller-to-controller data sharing model.

Update re: a question asked by Paul and Frederico back in March via slack:

* +*Paul's proposed temporary solution*++:+
!image (4).png|width=1104,height=466!
 to identify one of our company directors to avoid paying the 120€ fee
* +*Emilie’s response via slack (6 March)*++:+

Thanks for the email. [@beatriz.leiva|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U02T9DPTUCD] and I discussed this with [@alex.wong|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U01LHCFTNSX] and we all agree that the risks associated with this approach seem very high, both for Bolt Director and for Bolt:

* Bolt would be making a fraudulent statement to an administrative authority and the liability for lying to the administration is probably the same in PT as in other West Eur countries, i.e. very high
* The individual Director would be participating in a fraud and both directors are European residents, and therefore would face high responsibility, probably  up to emprisonnement sentence and they could be arrested for this + their personal bank accounts could probably be seized
* The fact that our competitors might have a similar process in place is not relevant, mainly because it might be that their directors are in the US / not in Europe, therefore not subject to the same risks

*In terms of next steps:*

* When do you expect product solution to be ready for the new user ID verification?
* We could start amending our Users T&Cs and charge a contractual penalty or pass through the fine to the user (still not clear from SPASS what's the recommended solution for PT - we're checking this with them).
* We could also check if under PT law, it would be reasonable to introduce in our Users T&Cs a contractual penalty as high as 300 euros, to cover the 199 + the cost of VAT implications (we'll be discussing this with TAX this week) + the loss revenue during the impoundment + the operational cost (we would need estimate from you on these costs please). This could then be converted to a 120 euros penalty when ID verif is available (and the fine is then 'only' 64 euros).

Let us know. Thanks

* +*SPASS advice:*+

SPASS just confirmed what we suspected with the solution you proposed:

The Portuguese penal code typifies _false statements made to public authorities_ as a crime (art. 348.º-A).
This crime cannot be committed by a legal person. Can only be practiced by a natural person.
In case Ahto is identified, he will only be held responsible as an accomplice if it is proved that he knew that his identification was being falsely used.
*_The person who identifies Atho commits a crime._*
*_As you know, to participate in public tenders is a cause of impediment for the competitor to have been convicted by final judgment for any crime that affects his professional conduct_*_. Is to prove this circumstance that time to time we have to request the_ *_criminal record certificates of bolt PT and its managers_*_._*_--> Also for this reason we consider that this situation is to be avoided._*

[^Bolt Mail - PT - Rentals - Proposed solution.pdf]

Modified Query 

{noformat}WITH
            count_of_orders AS (
SELECT
	ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_inapp_orders,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'cash' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_cash_orders
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id=etl.city_id AND etl.order_id=ot.order_id
WHERE
etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.state='finished'
GROUP BY
	1
            ),
            count_of_fraud_orders AS (
SELECT
	ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_inapp_fraud_orders,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'cash' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_cash_fraud_orders
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co ON co.id = etl.order_id AND co.city_id = etl.city_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id=etl.city_id AND etl.order_id=ot.order_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fraud_order_check  AS oc ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu ON uu.id = etl.user_id
	WHERE
		etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
			AND co.campaign_code IS NOT NULL
			AND ot.state = 'finished'
			AND ot.price_review_status = 'ok'
			AND ot.price <> ot.ride_price
			AND co.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND co.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
				                    AND (
(etl.user_price_eur <= 1 AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 500 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 60))
OR  
(etl.country_code = 'ng' AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 100 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 30) AND ROUND(etl.rider_discount*1.00/etl.partner_price,2) >= 0.45)
)  
		GROUP BY
			1
            )
            SELECT
	etl.city_id || ':' || etl.order_id AS KEY,
	1 AS fraud_campaign_code_cash_out
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co ON co.id = etl.order_id AND co.city_id = etl.city_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id=etl.city_id AND etl.order_id=ot.order_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fraud_order_check  AS oc ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id
LEFT JOIN count_of_orders AS x ON x.driver_id = ot.driver_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu ON uu.id = etl.user_id
LEFT JOIN count_of_fraud_orders AS y ON y.driver_id = ot.driver_id
WHERE
	etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
	AND co.campaign_code IS NOT NULL
	AND co.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND co.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
	AND ot.price <> ot.ride_price
	AND ot.price_review_status = 'ok'
	AND ot.city_id NOT IN (993,997,991,1167)
	                    AND (
(etl.user_price_eur <= 1 AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 500 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 60))
OR  
(etl.country_code = 'ng' AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 100 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 30) AND ROUND(etl.rider_discount*1.00/etl.partner_price,2) >= 0.45)
OR 
(etl.country_code = 'ng' AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 30 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 30)) -- Based on Targeted Campaign NGS12G6LX3HWB4R
)  
GROUP BY
	1,
	y.count_of_inapp_fraud_orders,
	x.count_of_inapp_orders,
	y.count_of_cash_fraud_orders,
	x.count_of_cash_orders
HAVING
	((y.count_of_inapp_fraud_orders >= 4
		AND y.count_of_inapp_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.count_of_inapp_orders, 0)>= 0.5)
		OR (y.count_of_inapp_fraud_orders >= 5
			AND y.count_of_inapp_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.count_of_inapp_orders, 0)>= 0.4))
	OR
            ((y.count_of_cash_fraud_orders >= 4
		AND y.count_of_cash_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.count_of_cash_orders, 0)>= 0.5)
		OR
            (y.count_of_cash_fraud_orders >= 6
			AND y.count_of_cash_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.count_of_cash_orders, 0)>= 0.4))
			        OR
        (y.count_of_cash_fraud_orders >= 10
			AND y.count_of_cash_fraud_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(x.count_of_cash_orders, 0)>= 0.3)
        {noformat}

Current successful payment flow:

# App send first request to create a ride, booking is being created.
# Payment-core receive first authorise request with new booking id, create a payment entity and call payment-provider-adyen /authorise endpoint.
# Payment-provider-adyen construct web-challenge URL and returns it (no interaction with Adyen happens).
# App redirects user to the web-challenge, user submit valid challenge, Adyen accept payment request (not authorised, just accepted), user being redirected back to app (or just browser closed).
# App send second request to create a ride, booking is already created.
# Payment-core receive second authorisation request with the same data as in first. Payment attempt entity is in pending auth state yet, there is no idempotent response in this case, request goes through to the payment-provider-adyen again.
# Cycle starts from number 3 and repeats until payment attempt entity state is not changed. This normally happens when Adyen send a notification that payment was authorised. Important that in this cycle only a single payment being done by user even if they submit multiple challenges, there is idempotency support in payment-provider-adyen and Adyen. Time to receive notification may vary, Blik AFAIK can take 30 seconds easily.

What we can do:

if for PAYG project we’ll recognise pending payment as successful, payment-provider-adyen will notify payment-core about authorised payment while user is yet on a web-page and when app will call to create the ride second time, response will be successful.

{noformat}with ride_fees as (
select

bdidr.city_id as city_id,
bdidr.invoice_id as invoice_id,
bdidr.vat_sum as ride_fee_vat_sum
from ng_public.billing_document_invoice_document_row bdidr
left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = bdidr.city_id 
where json_extract_scalar(payload_json, '$.lang_key') = 'ride_fee'
and bdidr.created >= cast('2023-05-09 07:53:00' as timestamp) 
and bdidr.created <= cast('2023-05-10 13:05:00' as timestamp)
group by 1,2,3,4
), 
toll_fees as (
select 
asc2.country_code as country,
bdidr.city_id as city_id,
bdidr.invoice_id as invoice_id,
bdidr.vat_sum as toll_road_vat_sum
from ng_public.billing_document_invoice_document_row bdidr
left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = bdidr.city_id 
where json_extract_scalar(payload_json, '$.lang_key') = 'toll_road'
and bdidr.created >= cast('2023-05-09 07:53:00' as timestamp) 
and bdidr.created <= cast('2023-05-10 13:05:00' as timestamp)
group by 1,2,3,4
)
select 
rf.*,
tf.toll_road_vat_sum,
bdid.order_id as order_id
from ride_fees rf
left join toll_fees tf on tf.city_id = rf.city_id and tf.invoice_id = rf.invoice_id
left join ng_public.billing_document_invoice_document bdid on bdid.city_id = rf.city_id and bdid.id = rf.invoice_id
where rf.ride_fee_vat_sum = 0
and tf.toll_road_vat_sum > 0{noformat}

Hey all. Just wanted to add some points about the market specifics and the experience we had in the past with the current rider-phone-number-sharing situations.

As Martyna had already mentioned - starting with the end of last year, the increase of foreign supply is clearly visible and increasing every month. This is causing quality and safety-related issues and we are focused on overcoming them.

In November, we experienced a huge media outburst that cost us a reputation in our market and raised questions about our trip quality and safety. All of this is raised from lost item situations where riders couldn’t get back their lost items because they couldn’t reach out to the drivers and at the same time, drivers haven’t noticed their lost items. 

From our perspective, the weight of responsibility for the rider’s lost item cannot be put on the driver and this is not quite logical to put pressure on the driver to contact the rider. The rider is the one who notices that his item is lost, and he/she should put the effort to find it, not the driver has to chase the rider and inform in which location they are going to meet. And we are also talking about the time here. Additional tasks such as contacting the rider, waiting for our messages, and taking responsibility for the lost wallet in the car consume the time they could spend ensuring that all other riders could get the service.

The second point here is - rider’s safety. How we can ensure that we will not increase the unnecessary contact volumes when we share the personal phone number of the rider? Riders are not feeling safe. This is why phone masking is applied. Consent to share their personal phone number with the driver could be impacted by the desperate need to get back their lost item. 

When we consider safety and contact - it is easier for drivers (and very common in our market) to have a separate SIM for Bolt. Also, there is a possibility for the driver to have a work phone (two phone numbers) while working with our platform and this can be marked in Admin, we do have a dedicated slot for that even if this is not included in the registration flow or driver’s portal, but I think that we could implement this if this is legally approved. If the permission is missing - why we cannot create a consent for that? If the driver does not agree - we will not share his/her phone number and would go another way, but knowing our drivers and the situations that are most common in our market - the majority of them will agree, Was this ever an option or there is more on regulations side why we cannot ask for their written consent related to this topic? Could you please explain more about this as I have maybe missed some updates on this topic - why the consent from the rider to share his/her phone number with the driver differs from consent received from the driver to share his/her phone number (sometimes, even dedicated for such happenings).

Do not get me wrong, I am not trying to prove that one or another approach is better or worse. I completely understand the risks and regulations. This is why I do stand in the position of “always contact the police”. I think that recommending the driver to go to the police station and leave the item there and at the same time informing the rider to contact the police is the best approach. In this way, nobody gets each other contact numbers. Our drivers are willing to drive to the police stations and leave the items there as it sometimes is on their way and they do not have to continuously contact the riders and agree on time-place specifics for returning the items.

CS contact, otherwise, is inevitable, but we could do more without putting much effort into this. Informing the rider at which police station the items were left seems enough. This requires a call to the driver, I agree, if there is no option to share the driver’s phone number and we cannot implement additional consent. 

Overall, our goals are 1) service quality 2) safety 3) less involvement with better ROI. We are noticing that the current process is not compliant with all 3 of these goals and would like to explore all possibilities for changing it and would appreciate your help in understanding what could be done differently considering the language barrier, back-and-forth communication, and personal data sharing.

Hello, 

Thank you for the ticket. 

I will give you an overview of the process live in Germany and how it currently works:

* The report comes in ([vehicle accident|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2407628971/Driver+In+Major+Vehicle+Related+Accident+Ride-hailing#Driver-in-Vehicle-Accident-Causing-Injury-or-Structural-Damage]/[unfit vehicle|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2404581840/Driver+Operating+in+Fraudulent+Manner+Ride-hailing#Not-Fit-for-Purpose-Vehicle-Use])
* The driver gets blocked and the investigation starts;
* CS Safety uses the templates in the screenshot (these are in German)
* Once the tool is filled in, the local OPS team gets a notification in a dedicated channel 
** The notification would look like the one you see in the screenshot
** It’s up to the local OPS team to decide whether the vehicle should be blocked, handle communication with the FO, unblock the vehicle, etc.
* When the investigation is over, the CS Safety agent removes the block from the driver
** No need to wait for evidence of car repair from the CS side, as that part would be handled between the local OPS team and the fleet owner

[Here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~62f27f32d49df231b6297bd4/pages/4361356159/DE+Safety+Ops+Blocking+Process+for+Local+Ops] you can find German Ops team instructions to contact the fleet owner, block the vehicle, etc. (it’s done by them, I asked if I could share it with you).

If this solution works for you, we would just need to have the templates translated into Norwegian.

----

Another solution we have in place in Portugal is similar but without Investigative blocks in case of an accident/unfit vehicle. Local OPS would receive a notification that the vehicle might need to be blocked but this is it. In PT this is done due to new regulations, but my suggestion is to keep the investigative blocks. 

----

Please, discuss it with your local OPS team, and feel free to schedule a sync next week or ask more questions. 

Cheers, 

Alessandro

{quote}Do you have a rough idea how much it costs (percentage wise), each additional consumer? We plan to have near term 4 consumers with later possibility to grow up (10-20 consumers){quote}

From our side we don’t care about how many consumers do you have. Very roughly traffic will cost $0.01/GB. So it heavily depends if additional consumers will read all the data, or just some part of the data from some topics. You can do some estimation based on the number I provided above. 



{quote}Who is responsible for splitting the topic into partitions? I would like to understand how many partitions will we have (tens or thousands), and if our team is responsible for partition count management or the SRE team?{quote}

Team is in charge of providing a desired topic configuration, SRE team is in charge or reviewing it and applying.

We have a dedicated [terraform repo|https://github.com/bolteu/terraform-kafka] where we manage topics as code. So the flow is:

# Team creates a PR in the repo. SRE team could help if you have questions about configs.
# SRE reviews the PR and applies it.



{quote}Ideally, the number of consumers (from a consumer group) should be proportional to the number of partitions behind a topic, in order to have load evenly distributed. How the team achieve this configuration?{quote}

It depends. 

If you rely on message key ordering within a partition, changing amount of partitions is not an option (it’s super hard to do in a reliable way, and pretty much impossible to do without changing producer/consumer configuration).

On another hand, if you don’t use message keys, or guaranteed order of keys in partition is not critical for you, we can increase amount of partitions on the flight. So we can adjust partition count to the amount of consumer you have. Very roughly, we use the next approach to set initial amount of partitions: number_of_brokers (most likely 3 in your case) * amount_of_consumers

Hey  [~accountid:6017bc19dc29b4006a7f1025] & [~accountid:6242fffc1da0e10071388193] please see below:

After reviewing the Memo from Arthur Cox on reclassification risks and considering the Dominos Pizza Case which is pending decision from the Supreme Court in Ireland ([[2019] IEHC 894|https://plus.lexis.com/uk/cases-uk/karshan-midlands-trading-as-dominos-pizza-v-r?&crid=f1da89de-f959-4c80-82a9-6135a02ce0a9&ecomp=tt5k&earg=sr0&prid=6307b57e-a6db-4401-ab61-c7505d628184#]) as well as the Alpha Cars case, I  think that Bolt are able to proceed with keeping in clause 2.3 in the Branding Agreement. If Bolt drivers decide to opt for branding their vehicle the branding would only be one factor of the following concepts: 

# Mutuality of obligations;
# Substitution;
# Integration; and 
# Terms of the contract. 

Bolt would want to ensure they have exclusivity (especially given that drivers are incentivised for having branding on their vehicle, moreover there has been instances where drivers multi-app and receive the benefit of the monthly fee from several ride hailing companies such as: uber, free now etc, but take the stickers off),  I think the exclusivity part of clause 2.3 is okay to remain in the agreement it will also circumvent the above occurring. 

The main reason I have come to this conclusion is due to the fact that this is a choice. Bolt are not forcing drivers on the platform to brand their vehicles (this would be completely different as this would be exerting control on the driver as this restricts the driver from working for competitors). However, in this scenario the drivers have a choice to opt in for branding (which allows drivers to earn more money) or they can opt out of branding their vehicle (which means the driver can have the freedom of having no stickers on their vehicle and are ‘free’ to work wherever they want). 

In the Alpha cars case it was a mandatory requirement for drivers to have branding stickers on their vehicles, however these stickers were magnetic so were easily removable, therefore could be taken on or off which meant the taxi drivers could take them off when they wanted to work for competitors. This is not the situation for the Bolt branding, once the Bolt branding is on the vehicle it is not easily removable until it is removed professionally (see photos of branding below). Distinguishing the Alpha Cars case, taxi drivers for Alpha cars had no choice but to have branding on their vehicles as this was a regulatory requirement from the local authority, whereas with Bolt drivers they have the freedom of choice, and ultimately it will come down to whether or not drivers want to opt in to receive the benefit of the monthly payment. Also taking into consideration that to be legible for the monthly fee the driver must ensure that certain conditions are met i.e. sending bolt proof monthly that the stickers remain on the vehicle. Again, whilst this may seem burdensome and may be construed as putting an obligation on the driver, it is a choice that the driver opts into this agreement. Therefore, if the driver wants to receive the benefit proof must be presented to Bolt (I do not see any issues with this obligation, as with any marketing campaign, to receive the reward certain steps must be taken). 

In the Dominos pizza case which is pending an outcome from the Supreme Court in Ireland the fact that the Pizza delivery drivers wore dominos uniform and the vehicles were branded with logos was only one factor the court considered. 

To summarise, I think that clause 2.3 can remain in the draft branding agreement. 

Please note, my note on this ticket on the 14 April 2023 contains pictures of the branding stickers. 

Please can you advise if clause 2.3 can remain or whether it should be removed.

* OPS think that asking drivers to drop the items off at a local police station is the best way (drivers are reportedly willing to do so). Better than asking them to coordinate the drop-off time-place specifics with the rider.
* The current CS process from OPS POV doesn't comply with the goals of the service (quality, safety, less involvement with better ROI).

*Things outside our scope:*

* _Ensuring that drivers help riders get back the items._ How do OPS look at encouraging drivers to cooperate with riders who want to get their items back?
* _Improving CSAT with a process update._ Riders are happy if they get the item back. Riders aren't happy if they don't. The only thing we may realistically change in the process is to explicitly communicate to the rider that we'll do our best to contact the driver about the item - but that the success of retrieving the item largely depends on whether we'll be able to get in touch with them. However, I don't have much confidence that this would significantly improve CSAT.
* _Determining what is a realistic CSAT for the lost items issue._ We understand that 85% is the global expectation for all issue CSAT rates. But is it realistic for the lost items issue (especially if we can't improve the process much)?

*Overall learnings about the current process issues:*

* Riders want to retrieve items. If they can't (for likely whatever reason), CSAT drops.
* CS can't force drivers to respond to our in-app messages.
* CS and OPS have different goals for process improvement:
** CS want to improve CSAT for this issue type. CSAT depends on the rider experience, which can realistically be improved mainly by making it easier and more likely for riders to get their items back.
** OPS want to ensure service quality, safety, and continuity. This means as few interruptions to a driver’s day as possible.

➡️ *Next to-dos:*

* Check if there’s any existing data about the state of the rider lost items issue in other markets or globally (perhaps Supportability has some data?)
* Check what sort of items riders typically want to retrieve (to see if they're valuables or small items)
* Check CSAT and issues with the current process in other markets
* Discuss the issue and potential global solutions with OPS and the Head of CS:
** _How do other market CS and OPS teams see this process and what issues do they experience (if any)? Are the issues different?_
** _Should we do a trial run by implementing a temporary process for LV and LT to call drivers and ask them to drop the items off at the local police station, then informing the rider about the item location)? (to see if it improves CSAT and rider experience)_
** _Wouldn't dropping off items at the local police station be an unnecessary burden for the police? Should this be solved within the company (Bolt)?_
** _Riders don't always leave valuable items; there may be small (not valuable) items they want to retrieve. Where do we draw the line for what items must be brought to the police station? (assuming that some riders may want to retrieve small, inexpensive items)_
* Discuss with the Head of CS the realistic (expected) CSAT for this issue type (can we reach 85% or should we expect it to be lower?)

The general rule is that even though the sale is performed via the Bolt app, the seller (retail) is responsible for the compliance, in particular:

# to provide true and comprehensive information on the beverages sold - therefore, we should have a disclaimer on the app *next to every seller* _"This online shop is owned and operated by [retainer] who is responsible for the sold products. All information about the sold products is provided by the retailer" (sample text);_
# to comply with age restriction criteria (beverages must not be ordered, solder and delivered to persons below 20 years of age) - we need an age verification; the couriers shall check the IDs (also, the couriers need to be over 18 years);
# the alcohol may be sold (including delivery) only between 10 a.m. and 8 p.m. on Mondays to Saturdays and between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m. on Sundays;
# issue documents for transporting alcoholic beverages to the address indicated by the customer, that is, the  invoice should be issued by the retailer and sent to the client together with the alcohol.

However, even though the responsibility is on the providers, *Bolt* as an agent offering providers a platform for selling alcohol *is bound by the obligation of professional diligence* to take reasonable steps to prevent law violations caused by the use of Bolt’s services. Thus, if we allow restaurants/stores to start selling alcohol before checking their license, in the worst case scenario within 24h (before we actually check them) a lot of alcohol could be illegally sold via the Bolt Food app. We cannot take such a risk.

Therefore, *providers shall not be allowed to sell alcohol through Bolt Food app before we have checked their license.* 

*Suggestion:* If the operations team needs 24h for the check, it is advised to introduce an approval process: providers upload the alcohol items → added items stand in the queue for verification (meanwhile, items are not displayed on the Bolt Food app) → Bolt operations team verifies providers license → if all good, items occur on Bolt Food app under specific provider.
Please note, that I have called LT consumer protection authorities to confirm the above. Also, I have written confirmation from EE consumer protection authorities that Bolt is responsible for checking beforehand whether the restaurant/store has the right to sell alcohol.

Hey again, [~accountid:62b1c880566f3e7b0a8f2eb7] 

I have no comments/objections to the last amended version of the Agreement. Please, find below the answers to the questions.

*_1. Clause 3.2 of Annex 1 - how do we calculate how many trips were made by the vehicles?_*

The trips will be calculated automatically in the Admin system and the payouts will be added to the Fleet’s balance automatically via an automatic fleet bonus campaign.
_Does the Contractor provide any kind of a report or an invoice?_
Thus, the Contractor has no need to provide any report or invoice.

*_2. Clause 5.2 of Annex 1 - should we establish the amount of fine in UAH considering that the currency of the Agreement is UAH?_*

Correct. Logically the fine should be in the same currency that the currency for payouts.

*_3. Clause 5.4 of Annex 1 - what is the purpose of this clause?_*

The logic of this clause is following.
Initially, according to the previous logic of the Agreement:
- Bolt invested a fixed sum into car purchase
- Fleet was obliged to perform during a certain fixed time (24 or 36 months)

Now Bolt will pay out this fixed sum gradually, in installments, according to the fleet’s performance.
It is highly probable that high performance will allow the Fleet to get the fixed sum faster than the fixed time ends, and the cars will be used then for another ride-hailing service.
This clause directly excludes such risk and obliges the Fleet to perform for Bolt till the end of the fixed time.

_Does this clause mean that in case the term of the Engagement ends but the Client still pays the funds to the Contractor, the Contractor shall continue to perform its obligations under the Engagement?_
No. The clause means that the Contractor should continue to perform its obligations till the end of the fixed time even if the Client has paid out the whole amount of the Fee stipulated in the Clause 3.1 before the fixed time ends.

_Or does this clause mean that if we pay the Fee the Contractor shall perform its obligations? Because we do not have the separate term of the Agreement, only the term of the Engagement._
Then we have to somehow stipulate the above mentioned principle of the fixed term’s priority above the term of the Contractor’s obligations fulfilment (the term of the Engagement) in order to exclude the mentioned risk.

[~accountid:610c07eb627b5600682f93de][~accountid:5cfe57d9a7095c0c3ffac38d]  I’m not sure how to proceed here. It puzzles me how only now we realise there are cash trips where the price is wrong and drivers might want their earnings. Sharing here some thoughts and questions

* Do we adjust on the driver’s side and take the loss? (considering we don't charge the rider since it’s cash) 
* How do we proceed in terms of receipt? Technically the rider did not “pay less”, they allegedly paid the upfront.
* Any change in the process is mostly a global change with financial implications.
* I’m not even sure how frequent it is, but I have a feeling it’s the type of process that each market is doing on their own.
* The “Route editor” process is redundant. Agents need to manually drag the route, check google, etc. It’s really not that complicated. To my understanding, it works like this:
** Base fare + Minute rate + KM rate + (other fees: LD rate, dynamic pricing, tolls, etc)
** All these rates are fixed by the country ops, the only thing changing is the predicted time & distance
** In the case of “Price is wrong” most likely Drivers took a different route (I’m not saying poor route but I hope you see where this is going 😄 ). This means different time and/or distance than predicted. The “comp guidlines” are saying that if it’s passing a certain threshold we would need to compensate.
** Ideally, Product/T&W would either implement “true price” in the backend or provide a calculator for the agents, where they simply need to add the final values (as opposed to the initial estimation)
* Upfront threshold double standards:
** Portugal has 30% threshold
** If a trip, after “price review” for wrong price ends up with 29% - by our process there will be no adjustment. Only after 30%
** If a rider, on the other hand, complains that “Driver took a poor route”, and the price is higher than expected by 30%, we generally trust the rider, compensate and adjust and/or block Driver as they “did something wrong”

Personally, I would reject this for now, as it’s a more complex topic that I feel you would bump into very soon 🙂 Please let me know your thoughts.

Thank you for your call earlier last week. 

As discussed, we needed to look into the following prior to Polina’s termination: 

# *What type of visa Polina was on and the rights attached to this, whether this was instigated by Bolt etc.* [~accountid:64182372c35660c269bb3412] thank you for providing the below this is very helpful. 
# *Whether we should pursue a redundancy or a settlement agreement?* My concern here related to if we were challenged on a redundancy matter and Polina said her role did still exist it had just been handed to someone else and she could prove this. I’ve spoken with external counsel on whether the best approach here is to pursue a redundancy conversation and offer 3 months pay in lieu of notice (which as discussed on our call would land softly) or a settlement agreement where we outline nothing relating to redundancy in particular, we simply just say it’s not working out and we wish you all the best in future with 3 months pay in lieu of notice (which we can do contractually). The benefit of a settlement agreement is that it’s the ‘belts and braces’ approach and if all goes well, an employee obtains their statutory required legal advice on the agreement, signs the agreement and they cant bring future claims against Bolt. With a redundancy, we are still open to the risk of claims, but our specialist has said if we can rely on this enough internally on structural movements it will be fine. On the other hand, if we took the settlement route and Polina obtains legal advice on the settlement agreement which she is required to under statute, her legal counsel could probe more on the circumstances surrounding her termination and draw certain conclusions surrounding fairness of her treatment and termination - whether evident or not. This leads me to my last point below. 
# *What do we do if Polina refuses to sign a contract of termination (redundancy or settlement).* Speaking with external specialists on this, they see there is still a risk to the business she can bring a claim later, but this is low and at the end of the day we are still able to legally terminate her employment via redundancy or settlement. If she refuses to sign a redundancy agreement or a settlement agreement, her employment will still come to an end and it will be up to her whether she wants to bring a claim later on the basis of discrimination etc - which based on my conversation with Markian is very low risk here and given she has been dealt with fairly as an employee. 

*Next steps*

Basically, for this to land well on a simple redundancy [~accountid:60420da05290e70069b64add] our employment lawyer  can give you some coaching on how to delicately phrase why we are terminating her employment and continue with your offering of 3 months pay in lieu. This way, if she does later bring a claim, it demonstrates you were going above and beyond what is legally required and gave her a gentle exit. Any future lawyer that picks up her case (if any) will be able to see this. 

To wrap this up, I’m going to coordinate a call next week with [~accountid:60420da05290e70069b64add] , [~accountid:64182372c35660c269bb3412] and our employment specialists Jen at Burness Paul so she can run you through the above for comfort on strategy. This will be a useful exercise not just in this instance, but something for us to be armed with in future instances like this for the UK.
